description: Pinned documentation and producer source code used to interpret the OGRDB fixtures in this directory, with the coordinate conventions they support and the conventions that remain unresolved. Digests cover the exact bytes retrieved; mutable URLs alone do not fix a historical interpretation.

statements: gapped: FASTA format with IMGT-gapped sequences
To download 'Source' sets, which contain all sequences without optimisation, append _ex to the format (gapped_ex, ungapped_ex, airr_ex).
The germline set is returned in JSON format. For human sets, the source set is returned.

In particular, duplicate sequences are removed and sequences inferred from transcripts are extended to their likely full length, as inferred from other alleles of the same gene, even if this full-length sequence is not fully supported by the transcripts.
'Source' sets, which do contain duplicates and do not have such extensions, are also available.
In the 'gapped' set, V- sequences are aligned and gapped, following IMGT conventions, whereas in the 'ungapped' set they are not aligned. Other sequences are identical in the two sets.
documents.observed_against_fixtures: The fixture bytes contradict the documented label mapping: the '_ex' exports are the ones that collapse identical coding sequences (one record naming the others as paralogs) and append 3' coding extensions, while the unsuffixed exports keep every identity as its own record without extensions. The producer code below does the same (extend=True when the format contains '_ex'). Endpoint names are therefore not treated as per-record guarantees.

statements: cdr3_start: CDR3 start co-ordinate in the 'unaligned sequence' field
unaligned_sequence: entire V-sequence covered by this delineation
j_cdr3_end: In the case of a J-gene, the co-ordinate in the sequence field of the first nucelotide of the conserved PHE or TRP (IMGT codon position 118).

j_codon_frame: Codon position of the first nucleotide in the 'coding_sequence' field. Mandatory for J genes. Not used for V or D genes. '1' means the sequence is in-frame, '2' means that the first bp is missing from the first codon, and '3' means that the first 2 bp are missing.
gene_start: Co-ordinate in the sequence field of the first nucleotide in the coding_sequence field.
gene_end: Co-ordinate in the sequence field of the last gene-coding nucleotide in the coding_sequence field.
Germline objects are referenced from airr-standards release-1.5 airr-schema-openapi3.yaml.

The website source code is published under a European Union Public License v. 1.2 and is available from GitHub.

producer_code.deployment_note: The revision running on the server when the fixtures were exported is not observable. The lines relied on below have been unchanged since 2024-04-08 (to_airr.py cdr3_start conversion, commit ae19d21) and 2024-07-06 (api.py delineation copy, commit 5ed6916); the fixture bytes are additionally checked record by record against the gapped exports.

lines.108-110: coding_sequence = coding_seq_imgt with '.' removed, plus ext_3prime when exporting an '_ex' format
lines.143-155: the IMGT delineation's unaligned_sequence is the same string as coding_sequence (gapped coding sequence with trailing gaps removed, plus ext_3prime when '_ex', with '.' removed); aligned_sequence is the gapped form
lines.166: 'cdr3_start': gd.cdr3_start - gd.gene_start + 1 (stored full-sequence coordinate converted to a 1-based coordinate in the unaligned/coding sequence)
lines.179-180: j_codon_frame and j_cdr3_end are passed through unchanged (no gene_start offset)

lines.339-343: extend = True when the requested format contains '_ex'
lines.349: AIRR JSON exports are built by germline_set_to_airr
lines.360: FASTA exports are built by descs_to_fasta with fake_allele=True
lines.542-578: served delineations copy the numeric fields only; unaligned_sequence and aligned_sequence are not passed on, so they are null in the served JSON

lines.246-247: cdr3_start: CDR3 start co-ordinate in the 'unaligned sequence' field

lines.1821-1825: default IMGT ranges over the gapped sequence, zero-based half-open: FR1 (0,78), CDR1 (78,114), FR2 (114,165), CDR2 (165,195), FR3 (195,312)
lines.1828-1868: delineate_v_gene: cdr3_start = 1 + number of non-gap characters in gapped columns before index 312, i.e. the first nucleotide after IMGT codon 104
lines.1203: bulk upload stores cdr3_start as a full-sequence coordinate: feats['cdr3_start'] + gene_start - 1

lines.87-91: fake_allele relabelling: '*00' appended to names without '*', '-' at index 4 rewritten (no fixture label is affected)
lines.98-105: gapped exports write coding_seq_imgt with trailing gaps removed, plus ext_3prime for '_ex'

lines.503-509: maintenance check (written for mouse V records) expects cdr3_start at aligned position 313 (1-based)
lines.552-562: aligned positions 310-312 are checked as the second cysteine

lines.394: stored cdr3_start: CDR3 start co-ordinate in the Full Sequence (V-genes only)

lines.163: J records are rejected unless (j_cdr3_end - j_codon_frame) % 3 == 0
lines.178: IgBLAST CDR3 end (0-based, last CDR3 nucleotide) = j_cdr3_end - 2

coding_interval.rule: sequence[gene_start - 1 : gene_end] (1-based inclusive in the record's sequence) equals coding_sequence, except where an '_ex' export appends a provider 3' extension after gene_end
coding_interval.exceptions_in_fixtures: IGH_VDJ.10 airr_ex: 23 extended V records; IGKappa_VJ.5 airr_ex: 1 (IGKV1D-8*04); IGLambda_VJ.4 airr_ex: 6. The unsuffixed exports have none.

j_landmark.rule: zero-based anchor in coding_sequence = j_cdr3_end - 1; zero-based coding phase = j_codon_frame - 1
j_landmark.differs_from: AIRR 2.0 prose (j_cdr3_end in the sequence field; j_codon_frame as the codon position of the first coding nucleotide, i.e. phase (1 - j_codon_frame) % 3)
evidence: In every J record of all six JSON fixtures (47 records) j_cdr3_end is smaller than gene_start, so reading it as a sequence-field coordinate places the landmark before the coding sequence.
The producer's companion tool treats j_codon_frame - 1 as the coding frame and requires (j_cdr3_end - j_codon_frame) % 3 == 0; all 47 records satisfy that check.
Codon check after the meaning is fixed: the anchored codon is TGG in every IGH J record and TTT/TTC in every IGK/IGL J record; it is a disagreement detector, not the basis of the rule.

v_landmark.rule: v_gene_delineations[0].cdr3_start (delineation_scheme 'IMGT', sequence_delineation_id '1') is a 1-based coordinate in coding_sequence naming the first nucleotide after IMGT codon 104; zero-based anchor of the IMGT codon-104 landmark in coding_sequence = cdr3_start - 4
v_landmark.scope: Records of the six JSON fixtures listed in sources.json whose label-identical record in the matching gapped export ungaps to exactly coding_sequence and has a complete codon at gapped columns 310-312. Every V record in these fixtures meets that condition. Other releases or sets are unsupported until the same checks pass.
evidence: Producer code: cdr3_start is converted to a 1-based coordinate in the delineation's unaligned_sequence, which is built from the same string as coding_sequence; the default IMGT ranges put it immediately after gapped column 312.

Record binding: for all 746 V records (IGH 209 + 202, IGK 82 + 77, IGL 88 + 88), 1 + the number of non-gap characters in gapped columns 1-312 equals cdr3_start, the codon at gapped columns 310-312 has no gap, and it starts at ungapped index cdr3_start - 4. All ten numeric delineation fields agree with the default IMGT ranges in every record.

Alignment origin: no gapped V record starts with a gap, and columns 67-69, 121-123 and 310-312 carry the conserved first Cys 23, Trp 41 and Cys 104 except in the records listed under conserved_position_exceptions_in_unsuffixed_gapped_exports, consistent with IMGT unique numbering starting at column 1.
The fraction of records with a Cys at the anchor is not used as evidence; non-Cys residues at IMGT 104 are reported as found.

gapped_alignment.rule: FASTA, header = provider label, '.' = gap, V records aligned to IMGT unique numbering with column 1 = IMGT position 1 and no alignment_labels; D and J records carry no gaps
gapped_alignment.matching: every JSON record has exactly one label-identical gapped record in the export of the same suffix, and the ungapped bytes are equal (IGH 249/249 and 240/240, IGK 89/89 and 84/84, IGL 98/98 and 97/97)

unresolved.detail: No source field states a V coding phase. Every V anchor is a multiple of 3, so a phase derived from the anchor is 0, but that is anchor-derived, not independent source support.
j_codon_frame converts to a phase, but whether the producer derived it independently of j_cdr3_end is not documented.
functional=false means the stored functionality string has no 'F'; it does not distinguish ORF from pseudogene.
Neither curational tags, functional=true, RSS adjacency nor exact context slices establish complete physical coding ends; '_ex' 3' extensions are provider inferences.
Free-text affirmation limits in curation notes use gapped numbering; no reviewed note interpretation exists for these fixtures.
IGHV1-58*01 (IGH_VDJ.10) declares v_rs_start 324 inside its coding interval 143-438, and IGHV3-38*01 declares v_rs_start 452 before gene_end 460; RSS coordinates are retained as observations only.
The deployed producer revision is not observable; conventions are bound to the fixture bytes by the per-record checks above, not by the code alone.
